description:
SPIDR child of task-78eedd8ebc2b43c581ac21ea28648a9a (architect-fa3a3e17, 2026-09-05), which measured far over the 10-file cap: it wanted a migration engine, a published command kind with full roster backfill, a real-PostgreSQL restore proof, three UI surfaces, a Playwright journey, a live drive and docs. This row is the ENGINE and the SAFETY PROPERTY. dependsOn child 1 (task-463f195efd2f4fd2886790029a474194, the migration tool) and child 2 (task-ff41c5c9efa34494b7b91e6f0ddcb7c2, the disposable-PostgreSQL lifecycle this reuses for the restore proof).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: applying pending migrations AFTER a `pg_dump` backup; the `moe-migration-receipt/1` record; the MIGRATION_BACKUP_FAILED and MIGRATION_FAILED refusals; and the restore round trip. NO command kind (that is the sibling publish row), NO UI, NO Playwright, NO live drive - all the parent's.

BACKUP BEFORE MIGRATE IS THE ORDER, and it is the only thing standing between a bad migration and lost production data. MIGRATION_BACKUP_FAILED must mean NOTHING IS APPLIED - a migration that ran after a failed backup is the exact scenario the receipt exists to make impossible. Assert the schema is UNTOUCHED on that path, not merely that a refusal was returned.

A BACKUP NOBODY HAS RESTORED IS A FILE, NOT A SAFETY NET. That is why the restore round trip is in this row rather than deferred: the row that writes the backup is the row that must prove it can be read back.

ARCHITECT RULING ON THE SHARED BACKUP TREE - binding on this row and on task-95e68a8dd2464e7b8ad4b1f8c4d2b2e4 (architect-fa3a3e17, 2026-09-06). The governor handed task-95e68a8d back asking for exactly this decision; recording it on both rows so neither worker has to infer it.

THE COLLISION, MEASURED. Both rows write pg_dumps under the same convention:
- THIS row (task-0a56ecee) writes a PRE-MIGRATION backup at `<project>/.moe-next/backups/<env>/<ts>.sql`.
- task-95e68a8d writes SCHEDULED backups under the same `.moe-next/backups` tree AND prunes them: its DoD 3 is "RETENTION PRUNES TO N and the receipt LISTS THE PRUNED REFS", with `BACKUP_RETENTION = 5` already exported from apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/activation-receipts-measure.ts.
Left as-is, a scheduled prune would delete pre-migration backups. That is not a tidiness problem: a pre-migration backup is the artifact a failed migration restores FROM, and task-0a56ecee's own rail 2 says a backup nobody has restored is not a safety net. One deleted by a retention counter it never knew about is worse - it is absent exactly when someone reaches for it.

THE RULING - SEPARATE SUBTREES, SCOPE-LIMITED RETENTION:
- SCHEDULED backups:      `<project>/.moe-next/backups/scheduled/<env>/<ts>.sql`   (plus the store backup)
- PRE-MIGRATION backups:  `<project>/.moe-next/backups/pre-migration/<env>/<ts>.sql`
